---
engine: markdown
title: "Statistical formats (SPSS, Stata, SAS)"
---

Files ending in `.sav`, `.zsav`, `.por` (SPSS), `.dta` (Stata), `.sas7bdat`, or
`.xpt` (SAS) are read with [haven](https://haven.tidyverse.org/). Point
`--output` (`-o`) at a `.sav`, `.zsav`, `.dta`, `.sas7bdat`, or `.xpt` file to
write one. SPSS portable files (`.por`) can only be read.

These formats store labels with the data. For example, a column with the codes
1 and 2 can carry the labels "Male" and "Female". haven keeps such a column as
labelled numbers, and `haven::as_factor()` turns it into a factor of labels.

## SPSS

Write a small survey with a labelled column:

```{term}
rush run -o survey.sav 'tibble::tibble(
  id = 1:4,
  gender = haven::labelled(c(1, 2, 2, 1), c(Male = 1, Female = 2)),
  score = c(7, 9, 6, 8)
)'
```

Reading it back keeps the codes and their labels:

```{term}
rush run 'df' survey.sav
```

Use `haven::as_factor()` to work with the labels instead:

```{term}
rush run 'df |> haven::as_factor() |> dplyr::count(gender)' survey.sav
```

## Stata

Convert the SPSS file to Stata. The labels come along:

```{term}
rush convert -o survey.dta survey.sav
rush run 'haven::as_factor(df)' survey.dta
```

## SAS

Write a SAS transport file (`.xpt`), and read it back. SAS keeps value labels
in a separate format catalog, so only the codes remain:

```{term}
rush convert -o survey.xpt survey.sav
rush run 'df' survey.xpt
```

`.sas7bdat` files are read and written the same way, but SAS transport files
are the more portable choice for sharing data with SAS users.

## Converting to other formats

Labelled columns become their codes in formats without labels, such as CSV.
Convert them to factors first to keep the labels as text:

```{term}
rush run 'haven::as_factor(df)' survey.sav | cat
```

```{term}
#| include: false
rm -f survey.sav survey.dta survey.xpt
```
